_label: SIMULATED. Targets for turning real London (LCL) homes into simulated Pune homes.
_source: Prayas (Energy Group), Pune: 'Insights from smart metering data' blog series, minute-level smart meters in about 115 homes, Jan 2018 - Jun 2020. Pages: energy.prayaspune.org/electricity-consumption-patterns, energy.prayaspune.org/electricity-load-patterns, energy.prayaspune.org/our-work/article-and-blog/temperature-and-electricity-consumption-patterns (accessed 27 Oct 2026). All watt values are Pune city sample averages per household unless marked.

published.ac_only_in_summer: ACs used only in summer, mostly at night; usually not switched on in February and early March
published.weekend: weekend daytime load higher than weekdays; night load not different

assumptions._note: Our choices where Prayas gives no number. State these in the paper.
assumptions.level_distribution: lognormal, mean 156 kWh/month, sigma 0.448 (puts the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles near 60 and 348)
assumptions.ac_homes_drawn_from: randomly from the top 60% of homes by usage level
assumptions._summer_note: date (MM-DD) -> summer weight, straight lines between. Zero until 8 March because Prayas says ACs are usually not switched on in February and early March. v1 used mid-month anchors, which leaked AC load into late February and failed check 8.
assumptions.midday_w: about 185-210 W outside summer (no published figure)
assumptions.year: LCL calendar 2013 is reused as a generic year; dates are not real Pune dates

profiles_w._note: Hourly watts (hour 0 = midnight-1am) for an average home of each class. Built from the published numbers above, gaps filled by the assumptions.

checks._note: Pass bars written BEFORE running the check.
